about: Version 2's test vectors (CRYPTO.md section 15), made by java/test/avpx/v2/CryptoV2Vectors.java from fixed seeds, and checked on every test run to be exactly what the server's code makes. Bytes are hex. Keys are given as the primitives take them: a P-384 private key as its 48-byte number; an ML-KEM-1024 key pair as FIPS 203's d then z (mlkemSeed, 64 bytes); an encapsulation as its m. handshakeA is pqIK (section 6): its player is the game's static keys, which A1's s sends sealed, and skemToPlayer is A2's encapsulation to the player's static ML-KEM key. handshakeA's steps give h and ck after every step (MixKey steps give the secret mixed and the k made), and its transcript is h after A3 (5.1, point 15). Its datagrams carry a stand-in cookie: a real one is the relay's own HMAC, and only it can check one. handshakeB is handshake B (section 8, and 5.1 points 17 to 20) the same way, joiner and host, with both identities and fingerprints, nJ and its commitment, nH, the transcript (h after B5) and the check code. Each side draws its random values in the order they first appear in its own messages. B's datagrams are end to end (AVPE), with a cookie of 0. handshakeB.refusals are whole B messages a side must refuse, by refusal number (section 16). sealedGame is section 9's sealed game datagrams (AVPG), sealed under handshakeB's split: the joiner's with keyJoinerToHost, the host's with keyHostToJoiner. result is "valid" or "invalid".

steps.step: start: h = SHA-384(the protocol's name), and ck = h
MixHash(the region, then a 0 byte)
<- s: MixHash(the relay's static P-384 key)
<- s: MixHash(the relay's static ML-KEM key)
A1, e: MixHash(the game's ephemeral P-384 key)
A1, e: MixHash(the game's ephemeral ML-KEM key)
A1, es: MixKey(ECDH(the game's ephemeral key, the relay's static key))
A1, skem: MixHash(the ciphertext to the relay's static ML-KEM key)
A1, skem: MixKey(its secret)
A1, s: EncryptAndHash(the player's static P-384 key, then static ML-KEM key, 1,665 bytes) (k at n = 0)
A1, ss: MixKey(ECDH(the player's static key, the relay's static key))
A1: EncryptAndHash(nothing), its tag (k at n = 0)
A2, e: MixHash(the relay's ephemeral P-384 key)
A2, ee: MixKey(ECDH(the relay's ephemeral key, the game's ephemeral key))
A2, se: MixKey(ECDH(the relay's ephemeral key, the player's static key))
A2, ekem: MixHash(the ciphertext to the game's ephemeral ML-KEM key)
A2, ekem: MixKey(its secret)
A2, skem: MixHash(the ciphertext to the player's static ML-KEM key)
A2, skem: MixKey(its secret)
A2: EncryptAndHash(the relay's session id) (k at n = 0)
A3: EncryptAndHash(nothing), the game's key confirmation (k at n = 1); h is now the transcript
start: h = SHA-384(the protocol's name), and ck = h
prologue: MixHash(the region, then a 0 byte)
prologue: MixHash(the joiner's relay port, 2 bytes little-endian)
prologue: MixHash(the host's fingerprint, as the listing gives it)
B1, e: MixHash(the joiner's ephemeral P-384 key)
B1, e: MixHash(the joiner's ephemeral ML-KEM key)
B1: MixHash(the joiner's commitment, SHA-384(nJ))
B2, e: MixHash(the host's ephemeral P-384 key)
B2, ee: MixKey(ECDH(the host's ephemeral key, the joiner's ephemeral key))
B2, ekem: MixHash(the ciphertext to the joiner's ephemeral ML-KEM key)
B2, ekem: MixKey(its secret)
B2, s: EncryptAndHash(the host's static P-384 key, then its static ML-KEM key) (k at n = 0)
B2, es: MixKey(ECDH(the host's static key, the joiner's ephemeral key))
B2: EncryptAndHash(nothing), its tag (k at n = 0)
B3, skem: MixHash(the ciphertext to the host's static ML-KEM key)
B3, skem: MixKey(its secret)
B3, s: EncryptAndHash(the joiner's static P-384 key, then its static ML-KEM key) (k at n = 0)
B3, se: MixKey(ECDH(the joiner's static key, the host's ephemeral key))
B3: EncryptAndHash(nothing), its tag (k at n = 0)
B4, skem: MixHash(the ciphertext to the joiner's static ML-KEM key)
B4, skem: MixKey(its secret)
B4: EncryptAndHash(nH), the host's key confirmation (k at n = 0)
B5: EncryptAndHash(nJ), the joiner's key confirmation (k at n = 1); h is now the transcript

refusals.what: B2 from a host with other static keys, sealed under the fingerprint the listing names: every tag checks, the fingerprint of the statics doesn't (the joiner refuses it)
B5 revealing another nJ, with a good tag: SHA-384 of it isn't B1's commitment (the host refuses it)

signatures.scheme: ECDSA P-384 SHA-384, r then s
ECDSA P-384 SHA-384, r then s

refusals.what: a handshake datagram of 1,199 bytes (A1's first, cut short)
a sealed control message of 103 bytes (the game's first, cut short)
a count of 4, for a length that takes 5
a byte after the last fragment's part that isn't 0
the game's first sealed message with a bit of its tag changed
the game's first sealed message with a bit of its message changed
the game's first sealed message again, after it was taken
